audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for women and artisans, Jabez birth-name and prayer, prosperity misuse, Egyptian royal kin, craft labor, royal labor dependence, Simeonite settlement, Hamite displacement, herem language, and Amalek violence.

verses.restored: Descendants of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah son of Shobal fathered Jahath; Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. These were families of Zorathites.
These were descendants/family of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, Idbash, and their sister Hazzelelponi.
Penuel father of Gedor and Ezer father of Hushah. These were sons of Hur firstborn of Ephrathah, father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari to him. These were sons of Naarah.
Sons of Helah: Zereth, Izhar/Zohar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz fathered Anub, Zobebah, and families of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was honored more than his brothers. His mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bore him in pain/sorrow.
Jabez called on Divine of Israel, saying, If blessing you will bless me, enlarge my border, let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm so pain may not rule me. Divine granted what he requested.
Chelub brother of Shuah fathered Mehir, father of Eshton.
Eshton fathered Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah father of Ir-nahash. These were men of Recah.
Sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. Son of Othniel: Hathath.
Meonothai fathered Ophrah. Seraiah fathered Joab, founder/father of valley of craftsmen, for they were artisans.
Sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Son/descendant of Elah: Kenaz.
Sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. A woman bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah father of Eshtemoa.
His Judahite wife bore Jered father of Gedor, Heber father of Soco, and Jekuthiel father of Zanoah. These were sons of Bithiah daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered took as wife.
Sons of wife of Hodiah, sister of Naham: father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. Sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
Sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er father of Lecah, Laadah father of Mareshah, and families of house of linen workers at Beth-ashbea,
Jokim, men of Cozeba, Joash, Saraph who ruled/worked in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem. These records are ancient.
These were potters and inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah; they lived there with king for his work.
Sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
Descendants of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; his brothers did not have many children, and all their family did not multiply like children of Judah.
They lived at Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These were their cities until reign of David.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five cities,
and all villages around these cities as far as Baal. These were their settlements and genealogical records.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah son of Seraiah son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi son of Allon son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah.
These named men were leaders in their families, and their ancestral houses increased greatly.
They went toward entrance of Gedor, to east side of valley, seeking pasture for flocks.
They found rich and good pasture, and land was broad, quiet, and peaceful; people of Ham had lived there formerly.

These written by name came in days of Hezekiah king of Judah, struck their tents and Meunites/inhabitants found there, devoted/destroyed them to this day, and lived in their place because pasture was there for flocks.
Some of sons of Simeon—five hundred men—went to mount Seir, with Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel sons of Ishi as leaders.
They struck surviving remnant of Amalek and lived there to this day.

translation_notes: Jabez's prayer is a single narrative, not a guaranteed prosperity formula, territorial entitlement, or method for forcing Divine blessing.
His mother's labor pain is remembered in his name; childbirth pain must not be treated as maternal failure, curse, or destiny for the child.
The request for enlarged border must be read beside verses 39-43, where pastoral expansion becomes displacement and killing.
Hazzelelponi, Helah, Naarah, Bithiah, an unnamed mother in verse 17, and other women interrupt the male-dominant list; omissions remain ethically significant.
Bithiah, daughter of Pharaoh, is incorporated into Judah's memory, resisting ethnic purity narratives.
Artisans, linen workers, potters, farmers, and people working for the king sustain the economy. Royal association may include dependence or coerced labor and should not be romanticized.
Verse 41 describes seizure of peaceful pasture and destruction of inhabitants. Herem/devotion language does not make displacement or killing morally clean.
Verse 43's Amalek reference may never be used against any living people or modern political enemy.
Several names, kinship links, and place identifications are textually uncertain.
safety_note: Reject prosperity-gospel formulas, territorial expansion theology, anti-Black misuse of Ham, ethnic cleansing, genocide, modern Amalek labeling, and romanticized royal labor. The quiet inhabitants displaced for pasture are not disposable background characters.
